u: Installs HPLIP printers and faxes in the CUPS spooler. Tries to automatically determine the correct PPD file to use. Allows the printing of a testpage. Performs basic fax parameter setup.
<dl><dt>Run in graphical UI mode:</dt><dd>-u or --gui (Default)</dd><dt>Run in interactive mode:</dt><dd>-i or --interactive</dd></dl>

<dl><dt>Automatic mode:</dt><dd>-a or --auto (-i mode only)</dd><dt>To specify the port on a multi-port JetDirect:</dt><dd>--port=<port> (Valid values are 1*, 2, and 3. *default)</dd><dt>No testpage in automatic mode:</dt><dd>-x (-i mode only)</dd><dt>To specify a CUPS printer queue name:</dt><dd>-p<printer> or --printer=<printer> (-i mode only)</dd><dt>To specify a CUPS fax queue name:</dt><dd>-f<fax> or --fax=<fax> (-i mode only)</dd><dt>Type of queue(s) to install:</dt><dd>-t<typelist> or --type=<typelist>. <typelist>: print*, fax* (*default) (-i mode only)</dd><dt>To specify the device URI to install:</dt><dd>-d<device> or --device=<device> (--qt4 mode only)</dd><dt>Remove printers or faxes instead of setting-up:</dt><dd>-r or --rm or --remove</dd><dt>Set the language:</dt><dd>--loc=<lang> or --lang=<lang>. Use --loc=? or --lang=? to see a list of available language codes.</dd><dt>Set the logging level:</dt><dd>-l<level> or --logging=<level> <level>: none, info*, error, warn, debug (*default)</dd><dt>Run in debug mode:</dt><dd>-g (same as option: -ldebug)</dd><dt>This help information:</dt><dd>-h or --help</dd></dl>

<dl><dt>USB bus:device (usb only):</dt><dd>"xxx:yyy" where 'xxx' is the USB bus and 'yyy' is the USB device. (Note: The ':' and all leading zeros must be present.) Use the 'lsusb' command to obtain this information.</dd><dt>IPs (network only):</dt><dd>IPv4 address "a.b.c.d" or "hostname"</dd><dt>DEVNODE (parallel only):</dt><dd>"/dev/parportX", X=0,1,2,...</dd><dt>SERIAL NO. (usb and parallel only):</dt><dd>"serial no."</dd></dl>

<dl><dt>Setup using GUI mode:</dt><dd>$ hp-setup</dd><dt>Setup using GUI mode, specifying usb:</dt><dd>$ hp-setup -b usb</dd><dt>Setup using GUI mode, specifying an IP:</dt><dd>$ hp-setup 192.168.0.101</dd><dt>One USB printer attached, automatic:</dt><dd>$ hp-setup -i -a</dd><dt>USB, IDs specified:</dt><dd>$ hp-setup -i 001:002</dd><dt>Network:</dt><dd>$ hp-setup -i 66.35.250.209</dd><dt>Network, Jetdirect port 2:</dt><dd>$ hp-setup -i --port=2 66.35.250.209</dd><dt>Parallel:</dt><dd>$ hp-setup -i /dev/parport0</dd><dt>USB or parallel, using serial number:</dt><dd>$ hp-setup -i US12345678A</dd><dt>USB, automatic:</dt><dd>$ hp-setup -i --auto 001:002</dd><dt>Parallel, automatic, no testpage:</dt><dd>$ hp-setup -i -a -x /dev/parport0</dd><dt>Parallel, choose device:</dt><dd>$ hp-setup -i -b par</dd></dl>

<dl><dt>1. If no serial number, USB ID, IP, or device node is specified, the USB and parallel busses will be probed for devices.</dt><dd></dd><dt>2. Using 'lsusb' to obtain USB IDs: (example)</dt><dd></dd><dt>$ lsusb</dt><dd></dd><dt>Bus 003 Device 011: ID 03f0:c202 Hewlett-Packard</dt><dd></dd><dt>$ hp-setup --auto 003:011</dt><dd></dd><dt>(Note: You may have to run 'lsusb' from /sbin or another location. Use '$ locate lsusb' to determine this.)</dt><dd></dd><dt>3. Parameters -a, -f, -p, or -t are not valid in GUI (-u) mode.</dt><dd></dd></dl>
HPLIP (HP Linux Imaging and Printing) is an HP developed solution for printing, scanning, and faxing with HP inkjet and laser based printers in Linux.
The HPLIP Launchpad.net site https://launchpad.net/hplip is available to get help, report bugs, make suggestions, discuss the HPLIP project or otherwise contact the HPLIP Team.
